nodes.name: Cathode ISG Coating
nodes.procedure: Commercial Pt/C catalyst ink was prepared with anion-selective PiperIon A-5 ionomer (40 wt%, defined as the mass of ionomer divided by the total mass of ionomer plus catalyst) in DI water and sprayed onto titanium fibre felts or membranes to achieve 0.5 mg_Pt cm^-2 loading. A thin carbon black interlayer was added to improve electronic conductivity, followed by a protective layer of activated carbon (0.08 mg cm^-2). For control electrodes without ISG, PTFE was used as neutral binder.

nodes.name: Anode ISG Coating
nodes.procedure: Commercial IrO_x catalyst ink was prepared with cation-selective Nafion ionomer (40 wt%) in DI water and sprayed onto titanium fibre felts or membranes to achieve 0.6 mg_Ir cm^-2 loading. A thin carbon black interlayer was added to improve electronic conductivity, followed by a protective layer of activated carbon (0.08 mg cm^-2).

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM images obtained using FEI Titan Themis microscope at 200 kV show uniform ISG encapsulation of Pt/C and IrOx catalysts.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) images were obtained using an FEI Titan Themis microscope with aberration correction, operating at 200 kV.

nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images were captured using a FEI QUANTA 450 FEG Environmental SEM, operating at 10 kV.

nodes.characterization_summary: Cl element XPS spectra show reduced chlorine adsorption on ISG-coated anode surface after OER reaction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) and chronopotentiometry tests revealed that ionomer-coated anodes significantly reduced chlorine adsorption and corrosion.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns show ionomer coating significantly suppressed formation of Mg(OH)2 and Ca(OH)2 on cathode surface during electrolysis.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis further confirmed this observation, with XRD patterns showing that the ionomer coating significantly suppressed the formation of Mg(OH)2 and Ca(OH)2 on the cathode surface during electrolysis.

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS in sandwich-cell configuration shows OH⁻ conductivity of Pt/C cathode layer increased from 4.12±0.96 mS cm⁻¹ (PTFE binder) to 12.31±1.95 mS cm⁻¹ with anion-selective ISG; H⁺ conductivity of IrOx anode layer from 9.40±1.08 mS cm⁻¹ to 18.43±2.66 mS cm⁻¹ with cation-selective ISG.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 1c, d, the OH⁻ conductivity of the cathode catalyst layer increased from 4.12±0.96 mS cm⁻¹ without ISG (prepared with neutral PTFE binders) to 12.31±1.95 mS cm⁻¹ with ISG, while the H⁺ conductivity of the anode catalyst layer increased from 9.40±1.08 mS cm⁻¹ to 18.43±2.66 mS cm⁻¹.

nodes.characterization_summary: Operando Raman shows ISG-coated Pt/C cathode maintains constant hydrogen-bonding features and suppresses Mg(OH)₂ and Ca(OH)₂ precipitation peaks vs. uncoated.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Operando Raman spectroscopy analysis was carried out... The results show that without ISG, the cathode surface exhibits strong peaks of Mg(OH)₂ and Ca(OH)₂, indicating significant precipitation. In contrast, the ISG coating greatly reduced these peaks.
